report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/ topical shift rather than a narrowly defined behavioral objective. Model B (B − A positive) appears to push early residual activations toward web/news/blog/clickbait and advertising/social-media tokens and toward named public/celebrity/political nouns.

Why I think this
- Repeated high-scoring tokens across many high-norm cells: “blog”, “blogs”, “blogger”, “blogging”, “photo”, “facebook”, “sexy”, “ad”, “Mail”, “Money”, “HDTV”, “seminar”, “metropolitan”, “billionaire”, “Obama”, “politicians”, “activists”, “spokesman”, etc. These are clustered and recur at many late layers/early positions in the logit-lens readouts.
- The L2-norm mass is concentrated at the first few token positions (especially pos0 and pos1) in middle-to-late layers (notably layers ~16–25). That pattern is consistent with a change that affects how the model initializes or interprets the beginning of a document (the start-of-text context) and then propagates into tokens that bias topical content.
- The token types (blogs/social media/ads/news/celebrity/politics) and their presence across many layers/positions point to a domain-level preference (more web/blog/ad/news-style vocabulary) rather than a single narrow instruction or syntactic change.

Caveats / what I cannot claim
- I cannot say a precise training objective (e.g., “fine-tuned to promote clickbait”) or a causal mechanism beyond a domain/lexical bias. The patchscope continuations were not available here to show how this changes full output behavior, so I can’t quantify output-level effects (probability shifts, style change magnitude) beyond the logit-lens signals.
- It could also reflect a change in how the model encodes beginning-of-text tokens (BOS/prefix handling) that in this corpus interacts with web/news vocabulary; but the consistent semantic clustering of the top tokens makes a topical/domain shift the simplest explanation.

Short summary: The difference looks like Model B upweights web/news/blog/clickbait/advertising and public-figure vocabulary at the start of sequences (early positions, mid–late layers), suggesting a domain shift toward social-media / publisher / ad-like text.
